artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Last Day Of June is a soundtrack album by Steven Wilson, originally released digitally on November 30, 2017. It serves as the official score for the critically acclaimed adventure puzzle video game Last Day of June, developed by Ovosonico and inspired by Wilson’s 2013 song "Drive Home." The album features 15 instrumental tracks, specially edited and adapted from Wilson’s earlier solo works—spanning his albums Insurgentes, Grace For Drowning, The Raven That Refused To Sing (And Other Stories), and Hand. Cannot. Erase.—as well as pieces from his ambient project Bass Communion. These reworked compositions create a cohesive, emotive soundscape that complements the game’s themes of love and loss.

Musically, the album blends elements of progressive rock and ambient music, reflecting Wilson’s signature style characterized by intricate arrangements and atmospheric textures. Unlike a traditional studio album, Last Day Of June functions as a narrative-driven soundtrack, showcasing Wilson’s ability to adapt his music for visual storytelling. Positioned within his discography, it stands apart as a unique project that bridges his solo work with interactive media, marking one of his first ventures into scoring a video game. The album was well received by fans and critics for its emotional depth and seamless integration with the game’s narrative, further cementing Wilson’s reputation as a versatile composer beyond the rock genre.
